title: Shapes: an abstract base and an interface
instructions:
## One contract, many implementations

Model shapes the way a Java program would, using JavaScript classes.

- `Shape` is abstract: `new Shape()` throws an `Error`; it defines `area()` (throws if not overridden) and `describe()` returning `"<name>: <area to 2 dp>"` using the subclass's `name()`.
- `Circle(r)` and `Rectangle(w, h)` extend `Shape` and implement `area()` and `name()` (`"circle"`, `"rectangle"`).
- An object is `Comparable` if it has `compareTo(other)`: make `Shape.compareTo` compare areas (negative, zero, positive).
- `largest(shapes)` returns the shape with the largest area using `compareTo`; `totalArea(shapes)` sums the areas.
hints: In the constructor: if (new.target === Shape) throw new Error("Shape is abstract");
compareTo: return this.area() - other.area(); largest keeps the shape for which compareTo(best) > 0.

checks.label: Subclasses implement the contract and describe themselves
Shape is abstract and compareTo orders by area

realityNote: In Java this is `abstract class Shape implements Comparable<Shape>` with `public abstract double area();`, and `Collections.max(shapes)` uses compareTo. The compiler enforces what the JavaScript version only checks at run time.
